chunks: Whosoever denies having once believed -- unless he is forced to do so while his heart enjoys the peace of faith -- and opens his mind to disbelief will suffer the wrath of God. Their punishment will be great,
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between forced apostasy and voluntary disbelief in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the distinction between *ikrah* (coercion) and *sharh al-sadr* (expansion of the chest), where the latter signifies a deep, willing acceptance of disbelief. While forced apostates retain their faith internally, those who willingly embrace kufr incur divine wrath, a concept often linked to the *Gharb al-Nafs* (lowering of the soul) in Alusi and Tabatabai's interpretations.
